extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, librarians, ALSC/Newbery committee members, and others preparing or evaluating American children's books for the Newbery Medal
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and eligibility rules used by the ALSC Newbery committee to judge and select the most distinguished contribution to American children's literature in a given year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme / Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual or moral substance of the book — what it explores, the ideas it puts in motion. Considered "the backbone of the Newbery award" — without strong thematic development, no work is remembered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate strength and development of central ideas; determine whether the work explores meaningful intellectual or moral concerns. A dominant, well-developed theme is essential to lasting distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Development
rubrics_metrics.description: How events unfold in service of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plot primarily for how it impacts other elements — especially character and theme — rather than as an event sequence alone. Look for plot that advances thematic and character development rather than merely providing action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth, dimensionality, and authenticity of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how well characters grow, change, or persist and whether they are recognizable as human (or as the kind of being they are). Consider complexity, emotional truth, and the role characters play in conveying theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Delineation of time period, location, and any world-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect setting to be specific and integrated with theme; it should serve the work's emotional and intellectual goals. Evaluate whether setting contributes meaningfully to atmosphere, plot plausibility, and thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of Style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether style matches the matter, the age range, and the theme. Style is judged not by abstract notions of "good prose" but by fitness for this particular work and its intended child audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, Clarity, and Organization of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonfiction or fiction with factual elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if information is presented accurately and whether it is organized so a child reader can follow. This criterion applies where factual content or explanatory material is part of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child Audience Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A book must be evaluated as a contribution to children's literature — appropriate to its intended age range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conceptual accessibility, emotional fitness, and imaginative invitation. A book that is technically distinguished but inaccessible to children does not qualify; ensure the work speaks to and is usable by its intended child readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Constraints (procedural, not aesthetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements the work must satisfy to be considered for the Newbery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work must be original; author must be a U.S. citizen or resident; book must be published in English in the U.S. during the prior year. These are eligibility rules rather than aesthetic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting Procedure / Scoring Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How committee rankings translate into points and winner determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members rank their top three: 1st place = 4 points, 2nd place = 3 points, 3rd place = 2 points. A winner must receive at least 8 first-place votes AND be at least 8 points ahead of the second-place finisher. These numeric rules govern selection after qualitative evaluation.
